question: Related Questions Q. I have a question regarding the validity of divorce if forced. I was forced to sign the decree of divorce by my mother after serious differences developed between my family and my wife's family over whether my wife, who is a doctor, should work or not. I and my mother (I am the only son and father has passed) were completely against my wife working after the birth of my daughter. My wife's family on the other hand were adamant that she will work no matter what. So one day when I refused to allow my wife to give a job interview, her mother came over and after a very hot exchange of words and abuses, she took away my wife with her, although I tried very hard and also requested my wife not to leave as I feared the breakup of our marriage. She had already spent about five months at her parent's house before my daughter's birth due to differences on permission to work and having a separate house. She came back to my house after our child's birth. After my wife left again, my mother pressurised me to divorce her but I kept avoiding it expecting my wife and her parents to relent on their demand. After about three months, seeing no compromise from my wife I sent her a text message that if she didnot come back within a week on the condition that she will not work, she will be divorced once. My wife agreed to come. But before she could come, my mother forced me to sign the divorce papers threatening that if I didnot do so, she would kill herself. She had attempted suicide before by taking sleeping pills on another dispute and I knew she could it again in my absence. She said it would be either her or my wife. My sisters, who are all married, also sided with my mother and said that they would cut off all realtions with me if I did not do so. Now being the only son and caretaker of the family I could not afford to let my mother die or strain relations with sisters. Besides my mother had brought me up like a father after he died when i was only six. I felt exteremely indebted to her. I told my mother that my wife had agreed to come on the condition that she will not work. But she was not prepared to listen to any thing and told me that as long as she was alive she could not see me with that woman. I was left with no choice but to sign the papers. answer: Social Matters >> Talaq (Divorce) Question ID: 48643 Country: India Title: Wife left the house without my permission on her own and living separetly since 10 months.Whether her act is marital discord and desertion. Question: My wife left the house on 09.12.2012 without my permission on her own for no reason (for the second time) though told to her that if she step out of the house there will be no returning back into the house and so, think twice and take her own decision to step out of this house and should not blame her parents/relatives that she left the house on their provocation and she must be wholly responsible of what she is doing. The religious elders whom I have called to speak with my wife’s parents and available at that time in my house also told her that when there is no difference among you both and living happily, it is not correct to leave the house on provocation of your parents, brother and relatives when your husband is not permitting you to leave the house. Hearing to all, she did not care and left the house taking my 5 months child and since then we are living separately. (1) My wife act can be termed as Marital Discord (Nushooz) and treat it as desertion. (2) Is she eligible for maintenance? Answer ID: 48643 Posted on: Aug 31, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 1346/D-276/File-D=11/1434) (1) Nushooz means to leave the house of husband unduly without the consent of the husband. قال فى الدر وخارجة من بيته بغير حق وهى الناشزة حتى تعود (الدر مع الرد ج 2، ص 702) If she left on the basis of her right i.e. she demanded her mahr and left when she was not paid or left to visit her parents on a suitable time then it shall not be called nushooz. انه الصحيح المفتى به من انها تخرج للوالدين فى كل جمعة باذنه وبدونه الدر مع الرد ج 2، ص 721 (2) In case of nushooz she shall not be entitled to receive her maintenance expenses, but the expenses of the child shall be wajib on father. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
